We’re happy to help, especially when you’re budgeting carefully.

To choose the best option when money is tight, you can:

Compare online: Online mattresses are typically more affordable, offer more choices, and let you compare prices and reviews easily.
Use our guides: We provide a blog on how to choose a mattress so you can match firmness, size, and features to your needs.
Consider size carefully: Twin or Full sizes cost less than Queen/King and may be enough if you sleep alone. Queen is usually best for couples; King/Cal King if you need extra space.
Match firmness to your sleep style: Softer (1–3) suits side sleepers, medium (4–6) fits most people, and firmer (7–10) supports back and stomach sleepers—this helps avoid paying for features you don’t need.
Look at payment flexibility: We support Credit Cards and PayPal, and also partners like Afterpay, Affirm, and Katapult so you can split payments over time instead of paying all at once.

If you’d like, tell us your sleeping position, how many people will use the bed, and the size you’re considering, and we can narrow it down further using these guidelines.

To get the best value for your money with a mattress (not the cheapest or priciest), we suggest:

Shop online for generally lower prices, more choices, reviews, and easy price comparison.
Choose medium-firm (4–6), which suits most people and balances comfort and support.
Pick a type based on needs:
Memory foam for pressure relief
Latex for bounce and breathability
Hybrid/spring for strong support and resilience
Select the smallest size that comfortably fits sleepers to avoid paying for unused space (e.g., Queen for most couples, Twin/Twin XL for one person, King/Cal King only if you truly need the extra room).
Watch for holiday or sales events and sign up for our emails/website updates to catch big promotions; new users get 3% off.
Factor in total cost, not just sticker price: our mattresses ship free and include a 100‑day free trial, but you may pay for old mattress removal and, if you return for non‑defect reasons, return shipping.

Using these points together typically gives you the strongest mix of performance, durability, and cost control—i.e., the best bang for your buck.

Whether the pricier option is “worth it” depends on your needs rather than price alone.

Materials & construction: Thicker or multi-layer memory foam/latex and better edge support usually cost more and can improve support, durability, and comfort.
Firmness match: A medium-firm (4–6) suits most people; heavier sleepers over 230 lb may benefit from a plusher mattress that still has firmness around 5–6 and durable materials.

If the cheaper mattress already meets your firmness, support, and comfort needs, it can be perfectly fine. Pay for the higher price only if it offers clearly better materials, support, or durability that match your body type and sleep preferences.
